name: flame_veil_blue
description: translucent blue flame veils crossing one another over a crisp fractal, their rims and one veil lit lemon yellow, on a deep blue ground
reuses: field smooth as scooped period sheets (fill 0.22, edge 0.12) screened in blue, one per view: the translucent sheets
a second period sheet per view, edge only, from the map's yellow end: the lit rims
glow_filaments' falloff hair on the frame's own de: the crisp set under the veils
the tone pass with log_density, at the reference's median and p10
adds: the `view` member of a field channel: the field read off its own escape loop at a turned, scaled and shifted point of the plane (and a moved `c`), so several views' sheets cross as flame veils
notes: Added: the `view` member of a field channel: scooped period sheets on the smooth count of four turned, scaled, off-centre views crossing additively, rims from the map's yellow end, the set a crisp hair beneath. Its structure, a thin set seen shallow with wide far field, is one the galleries lack (measured): its locations are hand-placed (step 4's exception)

Lessons: The nineteenth to twenty-second styles came in one item, from four flame fractals whose look is **veils**: translucent sheets of accumulated density crossing one another, lit at their edges (`bluebird-25.jpg`, `celestial-domain-25.jpg`, `cipher-25.jpg`, `chalk-drawing-25.jpg`). `glow_filaments` had reached a flame's threads but not its sheets, and the sheets went in as **one member**, `view`: a field read off its own escape loop at a turned, scaled, off-centre point. Everything else is old: per view a scooped period sheet on the smooth count (dim face, bright rim) and a second, edge-only sheet for the lit rim, screened over the frame's own, the set a crisp falloff hair underneath, and the tone pass with `log_density`. Four lessons. **One loop's level lines never cross**: every field of one orbit is banded along the same equipotentials, so sheets cut from one loop nest like onion skins; a second loop at a moved point has level lines of its own, and four such views' sheets cross at every angle, brightest where they overlap. **Views about one centre draw a tunnel**: a shallow set's equipotentials are near-circles round it, so views only turned about the frame's middle nest their rings into a bullseye; each view's centre shifted 0.2 to 0.4 frame widths off makes the ring systems cross instead. Far from the set the level lines are still arcs, which is why `cipher-25.jpg`'s S-shaped ribbons swirling through the frame were not reached: its style draws silky arcs (a fine period sheet per veil for the strands) round the set; moving each view's set off the frame (shifts of 0.6 to 1 frame width) sweeps the arcs across it instead, the nearest its round one came to the ribbons. Its first fit read p90 ~0.40 against 0.51 at most drafts, and brighter strands fixed that but washed the violet grey under `log_density`; the kept balance is bright rims and faint strands. **Veils need far field, which the galleries lack**: a gallery seat is a deep zoom of lace, where every view's bands crowd into texture and the veils vanish into it. The share of a 320x200 frame lying over 0.02 frame widths from the set reads median 0.285 over the scout's 40 gallery seats (5 at 0.5 or more) and 0.544 over 40 hand seats (23), so the locations are hand-placed shallow Julia sets, Misiurewicz dendrites and whole multibrots (step 4's exception), with those five gallery seats in the pool; whole sets whose basin is a smooth disc read as one ring round a blob and were dropped by eye. **Straight-edged panes are not level lines**: `chalk-drawing-25.jpg`'s shards are flat polygons, and the nearest escape-time shapes are the cross trap's star-shaped level lines (rank sheets through two views) and `shaded_blades`' strip blades, pointed and curved; over a Julia dust drawn crisp they give translucent shards with snowflakes embedded, a partial reach, and stacking screened sheets flattened the frame until the tone pass could not pull its p10 down, so the ground went near-black and every fill thinned.
